rationale: PY-D23 (round 12). A module-scope binding written by a statement that is NOT an assignment — `for key, value in PAIRS:`, `with open(...) as fh`, `except ValueError as err` — published NOTHING, so a read of one had no declaration to resolve against. The corpus row is measured: `wagtail/wagtail/snippets/api/v3/router.py:76` reads `mixin` inside a module-level `for` loop over `mixins` and was UNEXPLAINED as `references … -> mixin [instancecheck]` on the round-11 dump. POPULATION, priced with CPython's own `ast` before the code existed (`.tmp-py/price-module-bindings.py`): 351 module `for` targets, 98 `with … as`, 48 `except … as` in 283 files, and 13 `for` targets in class bodies — 516 names in total, of which exactly ONE carried a residual row (`.tmp-py/module-bindings-price.json`). `authoredBeforeAnalyzerRun` is FALSE and that is the difference from round 11: the code landed first here, the PRICE did not — the population and the residual blast were both measured before the walker was written, and this file pins what the shipped analyzer does with those shapes. The function-scope rows are the negative direction: the same statements inside a `def` bind LOCALS, which are not symbols, and their counts must stay zero or the rule has been widened into a fabrication. ROUND 13 EXTENDS THIS FILE with the one thing the differential exposed: a class-body binder is a MEMBER and is therefore addressed by name AND LINE, so TWO `for x in PAIRS:` statements in one class body are TWO members (pinned by `expectSymbolCount: x equals 2` plus a `contains` row at EACH site), while two module-scope `for single in PAIRS:` statements are ONE module Variable (`equals: 1`, the module half's measured per-name publication). `x` was the row that proved it: the truth oracle's per-site derivation reported `AnsibleUnwantedChecker -> method @L157` as MISSING while the analyzer had published that member at L141 only.

expectSymbols.name: key
expectSymbols.note: THE POSITIVE ROW, and the corpus shape: `for key, value in PAIRS:` binds both names in the module namespace, each published at the target's own position with `boundByBinder` naming WHICH statement bound it — the counterpart of PY-D18's `boundByGlobalWrite`, so a reader triaging the symbol does not have to go find the statement.

expectSymbols.name: value
expectSymbols.note: The second name of the same `for` target, read through the SHARED pattern walker — `for k, v in …` binds two, and `addPatternTargets` is the one authority on what a target is.

expectSymbols.name: fh
expectSymbols.note: `with open("x") as fh:` — the `with` spelling. Its target lives at `with_item value -> as_pattern -> as_pattern_target` (the shape round 10 pinned after nine rounds of reading a field that is null on every real node), which is why this reader calls `asBindingTarget` instead of guessing a field.

expectSymbols.name: err
expectSymbols.note: `except ValueError as err:` — python deletes this binding at the end of the handler, and it is STILL a module-scope name for every lexically visible read (and python itself treats the scope as the enclosing one). The fact published is the one the source writes; the deletion is a runtime detail nothing in the file's surface states.

expectSymbols.name: x
expectSymbols.note: CLASS SCOPE: a `for` directly in a class body binds a class ATTRIBUTE, so the class half publishes a Property with the class as owner — and, separately, the `contains` edges below. The scope rule is the walker's: a `for` inside a METHOD is that function's local and appears in no symbol table.

expectRelationships.note: The row the mechanism exists for: the call sits 37 lines below the binding. `bare-name-callee` is CORRECT and is not a bug — the name IS a module-level value and the reason code says its route is a bare name (not a local, member or dispatch). What changed is that the name now RESOLVES, because the declaration is in the store.

The class-scope half is a MEMBER, so it gets the containment edge every other member gets. `contains` resolves by name AND LINE, which is why the SECOND site is a second row rather than a duplicate: a consumer reading line 49 has to find the declaration written there.

THE ROUND-13 ROW. Round 12 deduped class-body binders on `(class, name)` and published ONE member at L42, so this line had no declaration at all — the differential's per-site truth derivation reported it MISSING (`AnsibleUnwantedChecker -> method @L157` in the corpus). The price for the fix is exact: ONE name in the whole corpus has more than one class-body binder site, and ZERO binder names are also declared in the same class by an assignment, method or import.

The REFERENCE half, pinned independently of the call emitter: `ANNOTATED: fh = None` at module scope names the `with` binding. A fix that reached only `processCall` would leave every annotation naming a binder unresolved, and this row is the falsifier.

THE SCOPE ROW. `for m, n in PAIRS:` inside a `def` binds LOCALS — python gives the function its own namespace — so the call is a local call and `m` is not a project-wide name. This row was already correct before the round (PY-D14's collector reads the same shapes through the same walker) and is pinned because the round edited that surface: if the module-scope reading were widened into function bodies, this code flips away from `local-callee`. TARGET SPELLING (2026-10-19): the local binding is published with the family BINDING_SEP spelling, so the arbiter verifies it as a CLAIM (bindOK column) instead of binding the bare name to an unrelated same-named declaration; the reason code stays `local-callee`.

The `with … as` local, same scope rule. TARGET SPELLING (2026-10-19): the local binding is published with the family BINDING_SEP spelling, so the arbiter verifies it as a CLAIM (bindOK column) instead of binding the bare name to an unrelated same-named declaration; the reason code stays `local-callee`.

The `except … as` local, same scope rule — and the one shape where a wrong reading is least visible, because the name is deleted at runtime and nothing else in the file would contradict a fabricated member. TARGET SPELLING (2026-10-19): the local binding is published with the family BINDING_SEP spelling, so the arbiter verifies it as a CLAIM (bindOK column) instead of binding the bare name to an unrelated same-named declaration; the reason code stays `local-callee`.

expectSymbolCount.name: key
expectSymbolCount.note: One symbol per bound name. A walker that published per container element rather than per identifier would report 2.

expectSymbolCount.name: single
expectSymbolCount.note: THE MODULE HALF IS PER NAME, and this row is the pin. Two `for single in PAIRS:` statements at module scope are one module Variable — priced at 70 such names in the corpus. It is a deliberate, measured deferral rather than an oversight: a module Variable has no owner, hence no `contains` edge, so nothing in the differential or the store's member channel disagrees with it, and making it per site would add ~100 symbols whose effect on the RESOLVED/AMBIGUOUS split is not yet measured.

expectSymbolCount.name: x
expectSymbolCount.note: THE CLASS HALF IS PER SITE, and this count is the whole point of the round-13 row: two `for x in PAIRS:` statements in one class body are two members at two lines, exactly as two `x = …` assignments in a class body are two Properties. A walker that regressed to `(class, name)` deduplication would report 1 and the `contains` row at L49 above would go unexplained.

expectSymbolCount.name: m
expectSymbolCount.note: FABRICATION GUARD. `for m, n in PAIRS:` inside a `def` binds function locals, and locals are not symbols on this family's contract. The correct reading is `local-callee`; a publication here is the defect.

expectSymbolCount.name: n
expectSymbolCount.note: Same, the second name of the same function-scope target.

expectSymbolCount.name: local_fh
expectSymbolCount.note: The `with … as` shape inside a function: the LOCAL half of the same statement the module half publishes.

expectSymbolCount.note: The `except … as` shape inside a function.
